expectation: Membrane-rimmed stain on B cells, DCs, macrophages and monocytes, plus endothelium and epithelium. It should be clustered in lymphoid aggregates or follicles, with scattered single cells elsewhere, and partly overlap CD14 myeloid cells.
observed: A: bright, compact CD40 patches in a few cores (one dense aggregate in the upper right), with dim or sparse signal in others. B/C: mostly dark with faint scattered signal, which is fine for a patchy population. D: bright membrane-like outlines around cell shapes next to dark nuclei. E: CD40 patches partly overlap CD14 (white) and some CD40-only areas, with moderate background haze.
why: CD40 forms discrete aggregate-like patches with membranous outlines, and it partly co-localises with CD14 cells, though background haze lowers the contrast.
